title: exx_cs_inv_thr needs tuning for heavy elements
symptom: For systems with heavy elements (transition metals, large auxiliary-basis sets), the default exx_cs_inv_thr = -1 (LU inversion) is unstable: the Coulomb matrix is indefinite or EXX bands are garbage.
root_cause: The LU-based inversion is numerically unstable when the auxiliary-basis Coulomb spectrum is large or near-singular, as with localised d/f states. The ABACUS docs state that when exx_cs_inv_thr > 0 the inversion switches to diagonalization, discarding eigenvalues below the threshold.
minimal_fix: Set exx_cs_inv_thr to a positive value. 1e-5 is the documented 'safe and commonly recommended' value; for a strongly indefinite matrix move toward 1e-4. Do not raise above 1e-4 for an insulator.
validation: Re-run the Coulomb PSD/Hermitian gate and the EXX band gate; the matrix must be Hermitian to roundoff and have no materially negative eigenvalue, and EXX bands must be continuous.
avoid: Leaving exx_cs_inv_thr at -1 for heavy-element systems, or raising it so high that the Coulomb spectrum is over-truncated.
source: ABACUS read_input_item_exx_dftu.cpp documentation; oh-my-librpa empirical-statistical-defaults card; ~/.codex sessions.
